name: Frequency- and level-selective saturation, exciter, bit/noise grit and small-speaker transition
goal: Choose and set distortion as a tone tool rather than blanket crunch: band-weighted saturation (less drive on lows, more on highs, with output gain compensation), threshold/envelope-dependent saturation so only loud parts distort, saturation-as-clipper for headroom, a pre-filtered overdrive exciter at low dry/wet for brightness, subtle bit-depth/sample-rate reduction with jitter for vintage-sampler glue, narrow noise-modulation (erosion-style) grit, restoring sub after distortion, and a small-speaker cabinet on the master as a transition effect.

source.title: How to use DISTORTION properly in Ableton Live: Tips & tricks for Saturator, Redux, Erosion & more

prerequisites: DAW or Web Audio graph with a saturator/waveshaper, band-split or pre-EQ before distortion, bit/sample-rate reducer, noise-modulation effect, overdrive with pre-filter, cabinet/speaker sim

inputs.name: source_type
inputs.description: sub-bass | drums | pad/chords | vocal | full mix

outputs.name: processed_track
outputs.description: Track with targeted harmonic colour and controlled level

steps.action: Add saturation drive gradually and turn output down by the same amount to compare at matched loudness; decide whether the post-saturation clipper stage is wanted (adds more distortion) or off.
steps.expect: Colour heard without a loudness bias

steps.action: Weight saturation by band: reduce drive on the low band so subs stay clean while upper harmonics remain (helps 808/sub cut through small speakers); push the high band and width for brighter grit. Avoid cranking the low band—sub content collapses.
steps.expect: Bass audible on small speakers, sub still solid

steps.action: Level-selective: use a threshold/waveshaper mode where only signal above the threshold saturates, or an envelope-follow control that adds more bias/drive on louder parts (tube-style).
steps.expect: Loud peaks warm up; quiet detail stays clean

steps.action: Clipper use: set saturation so peaks are shaved (e.g. peak meter drops ~6 dB with little audible change), then raise the track level by the recovered headroom.
Exciter: overdrive with its pre-distortion band filter aimed at the highs, low drive, low dry/wet, a touch of tone—adds new harmonics instead of EQ boost to dull or lossy material.

Vintage grit: subtle bit-depth/sample-rate reduction (old samplers ran ~12-bit at roughly 20-something kHz), small jitter; lower bits = noisier, lower rate = crunchy ringing. Or noise-modulation (erosion-like: sine, noise, wide-noise modes; width sets the noise band) at very low amounts; wide-noise adds stereo width.
steps.expect: Glue and dirt at subtle settings; obvious lo-fi when pushed

steps.action: After heavy distortion on bass, re-add/restore sub (sub switch or low shelf) because distortion thins lows.
Transition trick: cabinet/small-speaker sim on the master (small speaker, far/dynamic mic, mono) during an intro or bridge, then bypass when the full track drops.
steps.expect: Phone-speaker sound then a big impact on bypass

verification: Low band less driven than high band on sub material
Lo-fi stages audible only as subtle texture unless intentionally pushed
Cabinet bypass lands on a section boundary
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there. Numbers quoted are the presenter's approximate values, in the source synth's own units.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Vital/Ableton/Dune/Massive X/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for a Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth vendors named in the source video.
Product names (Saturator, Erosion, Redux, Pedal, Dynamic Tube, Cabinet) map to generic saturator, noise-modulator, bit/rate reducer, guitar-pedal drive, tube waveshaper, speaker-cab IR.
Web Audio: WaveShaperNode with oversample, band-split via BiquadFilters before shaping, AudioWorklet for bit/rate reduction, ConvolverNode with small-speaker IR for the transition.
